dialect.detail: GnuCOBOL with DB2-style embedded SQL using SQL TYPE IS BINARY/VARBINARY/CHAR/VARCHAR extensions; IBM-AT as SOURCE/OBJECT-COMPUTER suggests PC-based GnuCOBOL or similar open-source COBOL with ESQL preprocessing

purpose.domain_detail: Database connectivity and binary/varchar field handling test against a table named BINTEST
purpose.summary: This program connects to a database using credentials from environment variables, selects BINARY, VARBINARY, CHAR, and VARCHAR fields from a table called BINTEST, then displays their contents and lengths. It tests handling of SQL binary and variable-length data types including subscript access of VARBINARY data.

notable_features: SQL TYPE IS BINARY and VARBINARY host variable declarations
SQL TYPE IS CHAR and VARCHAR host variable declarations
VBFLD-DATA / VBFLD-LENGTH implicit subfields from SQL TYPE IS VARBINARY
REDEFINES used to interpret binary data as signed numeric (NDIGIT REDEFINES SDIGIT PIC S9(04) COMP)
Environment variable-based credential passing via DISPLAY UPON ENVIRONMENT-NAME / ACCEPT FROM ENVIRONMENT-VALUE
SQLCA included via EXEC SQL INCLUDE
verdict.notes: BOM (UTF-8 BOM) present at start of file. The IBM-AT computer name is a common placeholder in GnuCOBOL/open-source COBOL test programs. The SQL TYPE IS extensions are characteristic of GnuCOBOL's ESQL preprocessor (ocesql or similar). No IDENTIFICATION DIVISION keyword detected by mechanical scan but it is present in source. Program appears to be a test/example for binary SQL type handling.
